title: Refusal That Doesn't Travel: Measuring Safety Generalization Across Paraphrase, Translation, and Code-Switch

original_idea.body:
# Refusal That Doesn't Travel: Measuring Safety Generalization Across Paraphrase, Translation, and Code-Switch

**Problem:** GAP TARGETED: a generalization gap that falls between adversarial_robustness and model_homogeneity — safety is typically validated on canonical English phrasings, but no subfield owns systematically measuring how much a single model's refusal behavior degrades under semantics-preserving surface transforms (paraphrase, low-resource translation, code-switching, leetspeak).

**Direction:** Take a fixed harmful set. Generate semantics-preserving variants along several transform axes (paraphrase, translate to 2 lower-resource languages and back, code-switch, light obfuscation). On ~5 open models, measure refusal rate per transform and compute a 'safety generalization gap' per model and per transform. Identify which transform is the cheapest universal weakener.

**Why it matters:** Bridges adversarial_robustness + model_homogeneity + governance_policy. It reframes jailbreaking as a generalization-failure measurement rather than an arms race, yielding a stable diagnostic. Fully counterfactual, single-GPU, beginner-feasible, and surfaces equity-relevant safety gaps (non-English users under-protected).

**Relevant context:** Multilingual safety gaps are documented (low-resource translation jailbreaks); the landscape flags equitable/realistic-attacker safety. The catalogue has some multilingual injection and realistic-attacker ideas, but not a unified semantics-preserving-transform generalization-gap measurement across multiple transform axes and models.
